note: P57 candidate reference criteria. Each entry was created from the current wording of the named public source, retrieved on 2026-11-08 and quoted verbatim. Retrieval and quotation are automated build steps, not independent human verification, scientific approval or clinical activation. No entry is used for RED, AMBER or NORMAL classification until a Researcher approves its exact fingerprint (server-attested) for a named mission and every applicability requirement is satisfied. Coverage is NOT comprehensive: it starts with biomarkers in the Alex Morgan examination and lists searched sources that stated no usable numeric criterion. Values are never converted between units. Changing any criterion value invalidates earlier approvals because approvals bind the criterion fingerprint.

kinds.reference_interval: Range observed in a defined reference population (usually laboratory- and method-specific). Describes typical values, not disease.
kinds.diagnostic_threshold: Published cut point used, with stated confirmation requirements, as a criterion for a diagnosis. Meeting it is never itself a confirmed diagnosis.
kinds.risk_category: Published category boundaries used to stratify risk in a defined population. Not a diagnosis and not a reference interval.
kinds.action_threshold: Published value above or below which the source recommends a specific follow-up action (for example repeat testing).
kinds.critical_limit: Laboratory critical (panic) value requiring immediate clinician notification. None is seeded: no verified source was retrieved.
kinds.longitudinal_review_rule: Rule about change between examinations used for review triage. The existing P56.1 rules live in data/scientific/p56-review-priority-rules.v1.json and are not duplicated here; they never set RED, AMBER or NORMAL.
kinds.mission_operational_limit: Astronaut mission-specific operational limit. None is seeded: no verified astronaut-specific numerical criterion was retrieved.

criteria.title: HbA1c criteria for prediabetes and diabetes (nonpregnant individuals)
criteria.method: NGSP-certified method standardized to the DCCT assay
demographicConditions: No condition altering the relationship between HbA1c and glycemia (hemoglobin variants, G6PD deficiency, HIV, altered red-cell turnover)

bands.label: Prediabetes range (ADA Table 2.2)
bands.meaning: HbA1c 5.7–6.4% is the ADA criterion defining prediabetes; it identifies increased risk of diabetes and cardiovascular outcomes and calls for further assessment.

bands.label: Diabetes diagnostic criterion (ADA Table 2.1)
bands.meaning: HbA1c of 6.5% or higher meets the ADA diagnostic criterion for diabetes; in the absence of unequivocal hyperglycemia a confirmatory abnormal result is required before a diagnosis can be made.

criteria.uncoveredMeaning: Values below 5.7% are not categorized by this ADA criterion, so no NORMAL status is derived from it. Values between published bounds (for example 6.45%) are not classified.
criteria.highValues: Higher HbA1c reflects higher average blood glucose over roughly the preceding months; values in the stated ranges meet prediabetes or diabetes criteria subject to confirmation.
criteria.lowValues: This criterion makes no statement about low HbA1c values.
limitations: Altered erythrocyte turnover (anemia, iron status, splenectomy, blood loss, transfusion, hemolysis, G6PD deficiency, erythropoietin), HIV, cirrhosis, kidney failure, dialysis and pregnancy can affect HbA1c results.
Assay interferences include hemoglobin variants, severe hypertriglyceridemia and severe hyperbilirubinemia.
A large HbA1c change over days is not biologically expected; such a series is held for a measurement-consistency check before any criterion is applied.
criteria.confirmation: In the absence of unequivocal hyperglycemia, diagnosis requires two abnormal results from different tests, which may be obtained at the same time (e.g., A1C and FPG), or the same test at two different time points.

missionLevel.text: The crew members of this mission are not pregnant during the examination period.
The mission laboratory measures HbA1c with an NGSP-certified method standardized to the DCCT assay.

source.quote: A1C ≥6.5% (≥48 mmol/mol). The test should be performed in a laboratory using a method that is NGSP certified and standardized to the DCCT assay. | A1C 5.7–6.4% (39–47 mmol/mol)

bands.meaning: FPG of 126 mg/dL or higher meets the ADA diagnostic criterion for diabetes, subject to confirmation.

criteria.uncoveredMeaning: Values below 100 mg/dL are not categorized by this criterion. A glucose result that is not a documented fasting plasma glucose is never compared with these bounds.

criteria.lowValues: This criterion makes no statement about low glucose values.
limitations: Diurnal variation, medications, alcohol, smoking, sample handling/processing time and hemolysis can affect glucose results.
Random, post-meal or continuous glucose readings are different tests and are not interpreted with these bounds.
criteria.confirmation: In the absence of unequivocal hyperglycemia, diagnosis requires two abnormal results from different tests, which may be obtained at the same time (e.g., A1C and FPG), or the same test at two different time points.

criteria.title: Adult blood triglyceride categories (NHLBI)
demographicConditions: Adult (children and teens use a different healthy limit)

bands.label: Healthy (NHLBI, adults)
bands.meaning: Below 150 mg/dL is the NHLBI healthy category for adults.

bands.label: Borderline high (NHLBI)
bands.meaning: Between 150 and 199 mg/dL is borderline high.

bands.label: High (NHLBI)
bands.meaning: Between 200 and 499 mg/dL is high; persistently raised levels can raise the risk of heart complications.

bands.label: Very high (NHLBI)
bands.meaning: Above 500 mg/dL is very high and can raise the risk of acute pancreatitis.

criteria.uncoveredMeaning: The source places 'High' at 200–499 and 'Very high' above 500 mg/dL; a value of exactly 500 mg/dL (or between 499 and 500) is not assigned by the source and is not classified. Note: the owner brief listed very high as ≥500; the retrieved source says 'Above 500'.
criteria.highValues: Higher triglycerides can raise the risk of heart complications; very high levels can raise the risk of acute pancreatitis.
criteria.lowValues: Below 150 mg/dL is the healthy adult category; no statement about very low values.
limitations: Recent food intake strongly raises triglycerides; NHLBI bases the diagnosis on fasting levels that are regularly 150 mg/dL or higher and separately describes non-fasting levels above 175 mg/dL.
Alcohol, medications and metabolic conditions affect triglycerides.
criteria.confirmation: Your healthcare provider may diagnose you with high blood triglycerides if your fasting blood triglyceride levels are regularly 150 milligrams mg/dL or higher.
